messages:
acme-sre: Hey team, we're seeing streaming connections drop for users on our corp network when we rotate session tokens every 5m. Symptoms: SSE stream sends partial payloads then client reconnects and immediately gets 401. Happens only on our private deployment behind a corporate proxy (Windows-based edge).

Samir K: Thanks for the report. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl/netcat) and any proxy logs? Is the disconnect immediate or after a few KB?

acme-sre: Disconnects after ~8-12KB of payload. Browser shows eventsource.onerror then a reconnect attempt. Server logs show: 
```
2025-06-05T14:02:11.452Z stream-id=abc123 GET /v1/streams/chat 200 chunked
2025-06-05T14:02:18.789Z stream-id=abc123 token-rotation initiated
2025-06-05T14:02:20.012Z stream-id=abc123 connection reset by peer (proxy 10.0.5.1)
2025-06-05T14:02:20.045Z new-conn tried for stream-id=abc123 token=rotated -> 401 Unauthorized
```
We can reproduce with this curl: 
```
# long-polling SSE head
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <short_token>" "https://private-api.acme.company/v1/streams/chat?session_id=abc123"
```
When token rotates we get 499 or connection reset.

Emily R: Can you confirm the private control plane token rotation policy? Also which TLS termination + proxy are you using at ingress? (nginx vs F5 vs corp proxy)

acme-sre: TLS termination is at a corporate proxy appliance (BlueProxy v3.1). Our infra team says the proxy rewrites TCP segments and might be doing connection pooling. We use sticky sessions but the proxy terminates TLS and establishes new backend conn.

Maria L: Noted. Two likely causes: 1) token rotation invalidates the original SSE session and the proxy is reusing backend connection for the new client reconnect which presents the new token *without* cleaning up the old stream, causing race + partial chunk reassembly. 2) MTU/path-MSS differences + proxy chunking cause EventSource to see truncated chunk and try to reconnect while server still considers session active.

Chris P: Quick check: do you set Last-Event-ID or any resume headers on reconnect? If there's no resume token, our runtime treats reconnect as a brand-new session and will expect auth to succeed. With private deployments some token stores (KMS short-lived creds) can be briefly inconsistent during rotation, so new token fails.

acme-sre: We don't set Last-Event-ID. Client just does EventSource default reconnect. Browser console shows 401 only on the second connection attempt. First reconnect attempt (within 100ms) sometimes 200 but with 0 bytes and then closed.

Samir K: Can you capture a pcap of the failing flow (client -> proxy -> backend)? Also please dump the proxy logs for the timeframe. The sequence we want: initial stream open, token-rotation event, subsequent client reconnect attempt headers, proxy->backend reuse flags.

acme-sre: Attached pcap we uploaded to the support bucket (link removed). Quick excerpt from proxy logs: 
```
[14:02:20] client=10.1.2.3 connpool=keepalive reuse=yes backend=10.2.1.4 auth-header="Bearer <new>" result=401
[14:02:20] client=10.1.2.3 connpool=keepalive reuse=yes backend=10.2.1.4 result=RST
```
Looks like proxy reused conn and then RST.

Emily R: Thanks. Two immediate workarounds while we debug: 1) increase token overlap window so rotated tokens remain valid for 30s; 2) have the client set a small jittered reconnect (200-500ms) and include Last-Event-ID or our recommended session_resume_token header to allow resume flow.

Chris P: I'll open an internal ticket INF-4723 to track a server-side mitigation: the runtime can accept recently rotated tokens tied to an active SSE session for a grace period and tie reconnects by session_id cookie (for private deployments we can expose config flag allow_sse_token_overlap=true). That should avoid 401 races when proxy reuses backend conns.

Maria L: Also note corporate proxies that do TCP-level pooling + TLS termination can reorder or merge chunk boundaries. Recommend enabling chunked-transfer flush at smaller intervals (e.g., 1KB) on the server side as a mitigation for proxies that buffer until bigger segments. For Dedicated customers we default to 2KB flush; for Private we can expose configurable chunk_flush_bytes.

acme-sre: Will try overlap window and client jitter. One more question — do you have any quick check to see if the proxy is stripping trailers or modifying SSE colon-prefix events? We saw random leading ':' lines dropped.

Samir K: Good catch. Some proxies strip lines starting with ':' (they treat them as comments). If you can reproduce with curl against the raw backend (bypass proxy) and see the colon-prefixed keepalive events present, then proxy is the culprit. Use: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private-api.acme.company/v1/streams/chat?session_id=abc123 | sed -n '1,200p'
```
If bypass backend works but proxy path doesn't, forward us proxy vendor/model and firmware; we'll coordinate with infra.

OpsBot: Incident created INC-2025-331 for customer acme streaming token rotation issue; assigned to Chris P / Maria L / Samir K.

Chris P: Assigned. Plan: 1) confirm via pcap whether proxy connpool reuse coincides with token rotation 2) implement server grace-window flag for sse tokens 3) docs update with client recommendations (Last-Event-ID/session_resume_token + jitter) 4) follow-up with ACME infra for proxy config. ETA for a patch: 3 business days for feature flag, docs same day.

acme-sre: Thanks all, we'll try the overlap tweak and report back. :thumbsup:
